findings.location: leader-election shared engine pool starvation; every SIGTERM shutdown aborts; maintenance loops silently die
findings.line: 1342 (max_overflow=0); 1375 (async with engine.connect() in _run_as_leader — connection held for the whole run_loop); 1620-1648 (pool_size=len(_leader_loop_names)=16 while ~23 _run_as_leader tasks are created); 1799-1846 (23 cancel + await lists); 1847-1850 (await task catches ONLY asyncio.CancelledError); 1855-1859 (engine dispose + close_checkpointer/close_agent_checkpointer/close_chat_checkpointer — skipped on the failure path)
findings.finding: The shared leader-election engine is sized pool_size=16 (len of the 16-name _leader_loop_names tuple, main.py:1628-1648) with max_overflow=0, but ~23 _run_as_leader tasks consume it and each leader holds its connection for the entire loop lifetime. Beyond 16, leader tasks block inside engine.connect() until SQLAlchemy's 30 s pool timeout raises sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError; the exception is stored in the never-awaited task (no runtime log). At SIGTERM, shutdown cancels all tasks and awaits each; cancellation does not interrupt a checkout-blocked task, so the stored TimeoutError re-raises through 'await task' (main.py:1848), aborting the lifespan: 'Application shutdown failed. Exiting.' — engine dispose and all three checkpointer closes at 1855-1859 never run.
findings.evidence: EXECUTED 3/3 runs (SIGTERM at t+50s, t+120s, and on a throwaway-DB run): traceback main.py:1848 (await task) -> main.py:1375 (_run_as_leader -> engine.connect()) -> pool/impl.py:163 -> 'sqlalchemy.exc.TimeoutError: QueuePool limit of size 16 overflow 0 reached, connection timed out, timeout 30.00' -> 'ERROR: Application shutdown failed. Exiting.' /health returned 200 immediately before shutdown in every run ({status:ok, checks:{db:ok}, agents:85}). In the 120 s run only 19 loops logged 'Leader election: this instance is leader for ...'; loop:dependency_auto_dispatch, loop:bg_process_liveness, loop:lesson_store_refresh, loop:barot_temp_agent_ttl logged none. Code comment at main.py:1620-1623 claims the pool is 'sized so every loop can hold its own lock-holding connection concurrently' — false (23 > 16). Cross-ref H-4 (16-name tuple vs 20+ registered loops). Contradicts Audit 13's static shutdown verification (recorded per brief §1).
findings.production_impact: (1) Ungraceful teardown on every deploy/restart: leader engine not disposed, 3 checkpointers not closed, uvicorn exits ERROR; (2) leader-gated maintenance loops (e.g., dependency_auto_dispatch, bg_process_liveness, lesson_store_refresh, barot_temp_agent_ttl) starve and die silently on the leader instance — coverage shrinks with no alert because the exception is never retrieved; (3) CI cannot catch it: no test SIGTERMs a started app.
findings.confidence: High (3 of 3 executed reproductions with full traceback)
findings.recommendation: Minimal fix per brief §85: size the pool >= number of consuming tasks (+overflow headroom) or give each loop a dedicated connection; catch TimeoutError inside _run_as_leader (log + sleep(retry) + continue) so a starved loop self-heals instead of dying; catch Exception (not only CancelledError) per task in the shutdown await loop so one bad task cannot skip teardown; add a SIGTERM clean-shutdown test to CI.
